_comment: The narration record for the whole film, lifted from docs/storyboard-v2.
scripts/synth.py reads this and writes assets/sceneNN.wav plus the
timing files in data/. One entry per scene:
n        scene number (matches scenes/sceneNN.js and render.py --scene)
slot     the scene's authored length in seconds; must equal `dur` in the scene module
nora     true when Nora is on camera, so a viseme track is written
optional true for insert scenes that are skipped unless --include-optional
chunks   speech is synthesised one chunk at a time and each chunk is placed
at its `at` time inside the scene, so authored beats (a silent hold,
a bubble arriving) stay where the scene put them. Consecutive
sentences that should flow as one breath belong in one chunk.
phrases  caption-sized pieces of the chunk; word timings are aligned to

phrases: Hi, I'm Nora.
You might know me as your friendly help desk assistant.
Talia and I have been working on an idea
that starts with one simple question:
How can we make it easier for people to get the help they need?
Across Northpointe, many requests still live in shared mailboxes.
They get forwarded, copied to multiple people, and buried in long email chains.
People are working hard,
but sometimes we spend too much time managing the request instead of solving it.
Now imagine someone helping a borrower who suddenly cannot access the system they need.
They send an email.
A question comes back.
Then another.
While the request moves through that back-and-forth, their customer is waiting too.
Better internal support can have a very real impact outside the company.
That is where BoldDesk comes in.
We've been trialing it, and what we're seeing is worth sharing.
The idea is an enterprise support experience where requests are easy to submit, easy to track, easy to hand off, and easy to measure.
This is not about adding another tool.
It's about improving what happens behind the scenes.
The person asking for help can still email.
Behind the scenes, that email becomes a ticket that can be assigned, documented, and tracked.
For the customer, the experience stays simple.
For the team, the work becomes much more organized.
The portal gives employees one place to open a request and check what's already in progress.
It also holds a shared knowledge base any team can contribute to.
Answer a question once, and what one team knows becomes something the whole bank can use.
It's mobile friendly too. Someone can ask for help from a phone between meetings, instead of waiting until they're back at a desk.
Sometimes giving us the right information up front takes an extra thirty seconds.
But that small step can prevent a much longer email exchange.
Less back-and-forth.
Less waiting.
Faster answers.
Now, I'll be honest with you. Not every change turns out great.
For some people it is exactly right. For others, less so.
But even then, you learned something, and next time you know better.
Most changes land somewhere in that range.
Either it is better than what you had, or you find out something useful.
Both of those are worth trying for.
Managers can see what's open, what's waiting, where the workload sits, and whether requests are being answered on time.
And that raises a real question for Northpointe, one leadership should decide.
We could set a single standard across the bank, or let each team set its own, fitted to its work.
Either way, for the first time, we'd be able to see whether we're meeting it.
When someone is out, the request doesn't leave with them.
The team can see the history and what's already been done, so someone else can pick it up and keep moving.
That record is also a complete, printable history, start to finish, if it's ever needed for audit.
The goal isn't to make people work harder. It's to make it easier to work together.
BoldDesk can also connect with tools like ClickUp, carrying information into project work without entering it twice.
It can automate acknowledgments, routing, and assignment. A team can even publish its support hours, so nothing that arrives overnight goes unanswered.
Every task we automate gives someone time back for work that actually needs a person.
Down the road, AI could help summarize long support conversations so a manager or teammate can understand a situation quickly.
That would need careful security and data-governance review, but it shows how this idea could keep growing.
That is why this is bigger than a ticketing system.
It is a customer experience idea, an employee experience idea, and an opportunity to help Northpointe work better together.
It is all of us against the problem, not against each other.
BoldDesk could help us move from managing inboxes to managing experiences.
I'm Nora. Thanks for listening, and I'll see you at the help desk.
